1 /* unparse_stmt.C
2  * Contains functions that unparse statements
3  *
4  * FORMATTING WILL BE DONE IN TWO WAYS:
5  * 1. using the file_info object to get information from line and column number
6  * (for original source code)
7  * 2. following a specified format that I have specified with indentations of
8  * length TABINDENT (for transformations)
9  *
10  * REMEMBER: For types and symbols, we still call the original unparse function
11  * defined in sage since they dont have file_info. For expressions,
12  * Unparse_ExprStmt::unparse is called, and for statements,
13  * Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseStatement is called.
14  *
15  */

66 string UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::token_sequence_position_name( UnparseLanguageIndependentConstructs::token_sequence_position_enum_type e )
67  {
68  string s;
69  switch(e)
70  {
71  case e_leading_whitespace_start: s = "e_leading_whitespace_start"; break;
72  case e_leading_whitespace_end: s = "e_leading_whitespace_end"; break;
73  case e_token_subsequence_start: s = "e_token_subsequence_start"; break;
74  case e_token_subsequence_end: s = "e_token_subsequence_end"; break;
75  case e_trailing_whitespace_start: s = "e_trailing_whitespace_start"; break;
76  case e_trailing_whitespace_end: s = "e_trailing_whitespace_end"; break;
77 
78  // DQ (12/31/2014): Added to support the middle subsequence of tokens in the SgIfStmt as a special case.
79  case e_else_whitespace_start: s = "e_else_whitespace_start"; break;
80  case e_else_whitespace_end: s = "e_else_whitespace_end"; break;
81 
82  default:
83  {
84  printf ("default reached in switch: value = %d \n",e);
85  }
86  }
87 
88  return s;
89  }

1535

1582  {

1587  unp->u_sage->curprint_newline();
1588 
1589  p++;
1590  }
1591  }

1593 #if DEBUG_unparse_helper
1594  printf ("Leaving unparse_helper()\n");
1595 #endif
1596  }

2233  }

2235  // DQ (11/3/2007): Since "ninfo" will go out of scope shortly, this is not significant.

2237  // DQ (11/6/2004): Added support for saving current namespace!
2238  ninfo.set_current_namespace(NULL);
2239  ninfo.set_current_namespace(saved_namespace);

2243  printf ("In unparseNamespaceDefinitionStatement(): reset saved_namespace = %p = %s \n",saved_namespace,saved_namespace->class_name().c_str());

2245 #if 0
2246  curprint("/* Leaving unparseNamespaceDefinitionStatement() */ ");
2247 #endif

2422  // Handle the different sorts of declarations explicitly since the existing unparse functions for

3366 void
3367 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparsePragmaDeclStmt (SgStatement* stmt, SgUnparse_Info&)
3368  {
3369  SgPragmaDeclaration* pragmaDeclaration = isSgPragmaDeclaration(stmt);
3370  ASSERT_not_null(pragmaDeclaration);
3371 
3372  SgPragma* pragma = pragmaDeclaration->get_pragma();
3373  ASSERT_not_null(pragma);
3374 
3375  // Request from Boyanna at ANL:
3376  // DQ (6/22/2006): Start all pragmas at the start of the line. Since these are
3377  // handled as IR nodes (#pragma is part of the C and C++ grammar afterall)they
3378  // are indented for as any other sort of statements. I have added a CR
3379  // to put the pragma at the start of the next line. A better solution might be to
3380  // have the indent mechanism look ahead to see any upcoming SgPragmaDeclarations
3381  // so that the indentation (insertion of extra spaces) could be skipped. This would
3382  // avoid the insertion of empty lines in the generated code.
3383  // curprint ( string("#pragma " + pragma->get_pragma() + "\n";
3384 
3385  string pragmaString = pragma->get_pragma();
3386  string identSubstring = "ident";
3387 
3388  // Test for and ident string (which has some special quoting rules that apply to some compilers)
3389  if (pragmaString.substr(0,identSubstring.size()) == identSubstring)
3390  {
3391  curprint ( string("\n#pragma ident \"" ) + pragmaString.substr(identSubstring.size()+1) + "\"\n");
3392  }
3393  else
3394  {
3395  curprint ( string("\n#pragma " ) + pragma->get_pragma() + "\n");
3396  }
3397 
3398  // printf ("Output the pragma = %s \n",pragma->get_pragma());
3399  // ROSE_ASSERT (0);
3400  }

3925 // Determine how many "else {}"'s an outer if that has an else clause needs to
3926 // prevent dangling if problems
3927 static size_t countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(SgStatement* s)
3928  {
3929  // The basic rule here is that anything that has a defined end marker
3930  // (i.e., cannot end with an unmatched if statement) returns 0, everything
3931  // else (except if) gets the correct number of elses from its body
3932  switch (s->variantT())
3933  {
3934  case V_SgCaseOptionStmt: return countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(isSgCaseOptionStmt(s)->get_body());
3935  case V_SgCatchStatementSeq:
3936  {
3937  SgCatchStatementSeq* cs = isSgCatchStatementSeq(s);
3938  const SgStatementPtrList& seq = cs->get_catch_statement_seq();
3939  ROSE_ASSERT (!seq.empty());
3940  return countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(seq.back());
3941  }
3942  case V_SgDefaultOptionStmt: return countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(isSgCaseOptionStmt(s)->get_body());
3943  case V_SgLabelStatement: return countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(isSgLabelStatement(s)->get_statement());
3944  case V_SgCatchOptionStmt: return countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(isSgCatchOptionStmt(s)->get_body());
3945  case V_SgForStatement: return countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(isSgForStatement(s)->get_loop_body());
3946  case V_SgIfStmt:
3947  {
3948  SgIfStmt* ifs = isSgIfStmt(s);
3949  if (ifs->get_false_body() != NULL)
3950  {
3951  return 0;
3952  }
3953  else
3954  {
3955  return countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(ifs->get_true_body()) + 1;
3956  }
3957  }
3958  case V_SgWhileStmt: return countElsesNeededToPreventDangling(isSgWhileStmt(s)->get_body());
3959  case V_SgSwitchStatement: ROSE_ASSERT(isSgBasicBlock(isSgSwitchStatement(s)->get_body())); return 0;
3960 
3961  default:
3962  return 0;
3963  }
3964  }

4932 // DQ (11/7/2007): Make this a more general function so that we can use it for the unparsing of SgClassDeclaration objects too.
4933 // void fixupScopeInUnparseInfo ( SgUnparse_Info& ninfo , SgFunctionDeclaration* functionDeclaration )
4934 void
4935 fixupScopeInUnparseInfo ( SgUnparse_Info& ninfo , SgDeclarationStatement* declarationStatement )
4936  {
4937  // DQ (11/3/2007): This resets the current scope stored in the SgUnparse_Info object so that the name qualification will work properly.
4938  // It used to be that this would be the scope of the caller (which for unparsing the function prototype would be the outer scope (OK),
4939  // but for function definitions would be the scope of the function definition (VERY BAD). Because of a previous bug (just fixed) in the
4940  // SgStatement::get_scope() function, the scope of the SgFunctionDefinition would be set to the parent of the SgFunctionDeclaration
4941  // (structural) instead of the scope of the SgFunctionDeclaration (semantics). It is the perfect example of two bugs working together
4942  // to be almost always correct :-). Note that "ninfo" will go out of scope, so we don't have to reset it at the end of this function.
4943  // Note that that it is FROM this scope that the name qualification is computed, so this is structural, not semantic.
4944 
4945  // DQ (11/9/2007): If we want to force the use of qualified names then don't reset the internal scope (required for new ROSE Doxygen
4946  // documentation generator).
4947  if (ninfo.forceQualifiedNames() == false)
4948  {
4949  SgScopeStatement* currentScope = isSgScopeStatement(declarationStatement->get_parent());
4950 
4951  if (currentScope == NULL)
4952  {
4953  // printf ("In fixupScopeInUnparseInfo(): declarationStatement = %p = %s = %s \n",declarationStatement,declarationStatement->class_name().c_str(),SageInterface::get_name(declarationStatement).c_str());
4954  SgNode* parentOfFunctionDeclaration = declarationStatement->get_parent();
4955  ASSERT_not_null(parentOfFunctionDeclaration);
4956 
4957  switch (parentOfFunctionDeclaration->variantT())
4958  {
4959  // This is one way that the funcdecl_stmt->get_parent() can not be a SgScopeStatement (there might be a few more!)
4960  case V_SgTemplateInstantiationDirectiveStatement:
4961  {
4962  SgTemplateInstantiationDirectiveStatement* directive = isSgTemplateInstantiationDirectiveStatement(parentOfFunctionDeclaration);
4963  ASSERT_not_null(directive);
4964  // currentScope = isSgScopeStatement(funcdecl_stmt->get_parent()->get_parent());
4965  currentScope = directive->get_scope();
4966  break;
4967  }
4968 
4969  case V_SgVariableDeclaration:
4970  {
4971  SgVariableDeclaration* variableDeclaration = isSgVariableDeclaration(parentOfFunctionDeclaration);
4972  ASSERT_not_null(variableDeclaration);
4973  // currentScope = isSgScopeStatement(funcdecl_stmt->get_parent()->get_parent());
4974  currentScope = variableDeclaration->get_scope();
4975  break;
4976  }
4977

5054  {

5056  ASSERT_not_null(function_definition);

5059

5061  ASSERT_not_null(function_parameter_list);
5062 
5063  if (function_body != NULL)
5064  {
5065  unparseStatementFromTokenStream (stmt, function_parameter_list, e_token_subsequence_start, e_token_subsequence_end, info);
5066  unparseStatementFromTokenStream (function_definition, e_leading_whitespace_start, e_leading_whitespace_end, info);
5067  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
5068  unparseStatement(function_body, info);
5069  }
5070  else
5071  {
5072  // We need to handle the case of a function prototype.
5073  printf ("We need to handle the case of a function prototype \n");
5074  ROSE_ABORT();
5075  }
5076 
5077  return;
5078  }
5079 #endif

5081  // DQ (1/19/2014): Adding support for attributes that must be prefixed to the function declarations (e.g. "__attribute__((regnum(3)))").
5082  // It is output here for non-defining declarations, but in unparseFuncDefnStmt() function for the attribute to be associated with the defining declaration.

5085  {
5086  unp->u_sage->printPrefixAttributes(funcdecl_stmt,info);
5087  }
5088 
5089  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
5090 
5091  fixupScopeInUnparseInfo (ninfo,funcdecl_stmt);
5092 
5093  if ( (funcdecl_stmt->isForward() == false) && (funcdecl_stmt->get_definition() != NULL) && (info.SkipFunctionDefinition() == false) )
5094  {
5095  unparseStatement(funcdecl_stmt->get_definition(), info);
5096  }
5097  else
5098  {
5099  SgClassDefinition *cdefn = isSgClassDefinition(funcdecl_stmt->get_parent());
5100  if (cdefn && cdefn->get_declaration()->get_class_type() == SgClassDeclaration::e_class)
5101  {
5102  ninfo.set_CheckAccess();
5103  }
5104 
5105  ninfo.set_SkipClassDefinition();
5106  ninfo.set_SkipEnumDefinition();
5107 
5108  SgStorageModifier & storage = funcdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().get_storageModifier();
5109  if (storage.isAsm() == true)
5110  {
5111  curprint("__asm__ ");
5112  }
5113 
5114  unp->u_sage->printSpecifier(funcdecl_stmt, ninfo);
5115 
5116  unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo(stmt, info, PreprocessingInfo::inside);
5117  ninfo.unset_CheckAccess();
5118  info.set_access_attribute(ninfo.get_access_attribute());
5119 
5120  SgType *rtype = funcdecl_stmt->get_orig_return_type();
5121  if (!rtype)
5122  {
5123  rtype = funcdecl_stmt->get_type()->get_return_type();
5124  }
5125  ninfo.set_isTypeFirstPart();
5126 
5127  SgUnparse_Info ninfo_for_type(ninfo);
5128  if (funcdecl_stmt->get_requiresNameQualificationOnReturnType() == true)
5129  {
5130  ninfo_for_type.set_requiresGlobalNameQualification();
5131  }
5132 
5133  ninfo_for_type.set_reference_node_for_qualification(funcdecl_stmt);
5134  ASSERT_not_null(ninfo_for_type.get_reference_node_for_qualification());
5135 
5136  ninfo_for_type.set_name_qualification_length(funcdecl_stmt->get_name_qualification_length_for_return_type());

5138  ninfo_for_type.set_type_elaboration_required(funcdecl_stmt->get_type_elaboration_required_for_return_type());
5139 
5140  unp->u_type->unparseType(rtype, ninfo_for_type);
5141 
5142  if (funcdecl_stmt->isForward() == false)
5143  {
5144  unp->u_sage->printAttributes(funcdecl_stmt,info);
5145  }
5146  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(NULL);
5147  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(funcdecl_stmt);
5148 
5149  if (funcdecl_stmt->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration() != NULL)
5150  {
5151  SgFunctionDeclaration* firstNondefiningFunction = isSgFunctionDeclaration(funcdecl_stmt->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration());
5152  ASSERT_not_null(firstNondefiningFunction);
5153  ASSERT_not_null(firstNondefiningFunction->get_firstNondefiningDeclaration());
5154  ASSERT_not_null(TransformationSupport::getSourceFile(funcdecl_stmt));
5155  ASSERT_not_null(TransformationSupport::getSourceFile(firstNondefiningFunction));
5156  }
5157 
5158  unparse_helper(funcdecl_stmt, ninfo);
5159 
5160  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(NULL);
5161  ninfo.set_isTypeSecondPart();
5162  unp->u_type->unparseType(rtype, ninfo);
5163 
5164  if (funcdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().isThrow())
5165  {
5166  const SgTypePtrList& exceptionSpecifierList = funcdecl_stmt->get_exceptionSpecification();
5167  info.set_reference_node_for_qualification(funcdecl_stmt);
5168  unparseExceptionSpecification(exceptionSpecifierList,info);
5169  info.set_reference_node_for_qualification(NULL);
5170  }
5171 
5172  if (funcdecl_stmt->get_asm_name().empty() == false)
5173  {
5174  curprint(" __asm__ (\"");
5175  curprint( funcdecl_stmt->get_asm_name() );
5176  curprint( string("\")"));
5177  }
5178 
5179  if (funcdecl_stmt->isForward() && !ninfo.SkipSemiColon())
5180  {
5181  unp->u_sage->printAttributes(funcdecl_stmt,info);
5182  unp->u_sage->printAttributesForType(funcdecl_stmt,info);
5183 
5184  curprint(";");
5185  }
5186  }
5187 
5188  if (info.AddSemiColonAfterDeclaration())
5189  {
5190  curprint (";");
5191  }
5192 
5193 #if DEBUG_unparseFuncDeclStmt
5194  printf ("Leave Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseFuncDeclStmt\n");
5195 #endif
5196 
5197  }

5553 string
5554 Unparse_ExprStmt::trimGlobalScopeQualifier ( string qualifiedName )
5555  {
5557 
5558  // DQ (10/11/2006): Now that we use fully qualified names in most places we need this
5559  // editing to remove the leading global qualifier (once again!).
5560 
5561  // DQ (8/25/2005): This is the case where we previously named the global scope as "::"
5562  // within name qualification. This was done to handle test2005_144.C but it broke
5563  // test2004_80.C So we have moved to an explicit marking of IR nodes using global scope
5564  // qualification (since it clearly seems to be required).
5565  // For member functions we need to remove the leading "::" since GNU g++ can't always handle it for member functions
5566  string s = qualifiedName;
5567  size_t subStringLocationOfScopeQualifier = s.find("::");
5568  // printf ("Location of member function substring = %d \n",subStringLocationOfScopeQualifier);
5569  if (subStringLocationOfScopeQualifier == 0)
5570  {
5571  // printf ("Found global scope qualifier at start of function or member function name qualification \n");
5572  s.replace(s.find("::"),2,"");
5573 
5574  // reset the string in scopename!
5575  qualifiedName = s.c_str();
5576  }
5577 
5578  return qualifiedName;
5579  }

5825 void
5826 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseMFuncDeclStmt(SgStatement* stmt, SgUnparse_Info& info)
5827  {
5828  SgMemberFunctionDeclaration* mfuncdecl_stmt = isSgMemberFunctionDeclaration(stmt);
5829  ASSERT_not_null(mfuncdecl_stmt);
5830 
5831 #if DEBUG_unparseMFuncDeclStmt
5832  printf ("Enter Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseMFuncDeclStmt\n");
5833  printf (" stmt = %p = %s\n", stmt, stmt->class_name().c_str());
5834 #endif
5835 
5836 #if ENABLE_unparsedPartiallyUsingTokenStream
5837  // DQ (10/26/2018): We might not need this code now that I have fixed a cut and paste error
5838  // in the latest debugging of the unparseStatementFromTokenStream() function.
5839  // DQ (10/25/2018): Test for if we have unparsed partially using the token stream.
5840  // If so then we don't want to unparse this syntax, if not then we require this syntax.
5841  bool saved_unparsedPartiallyUsingTokenStream = info.unparsedPartiallyUsingTokenStream();
5842  if (saved_unparsedPartiallyUsingTokenStream == true)
5843  {
5844  SgFunctionDefinition* function_definition = mfuncdecl_stmt->get_definition();
5845  ASSERT_not_null(function_definition);
5846  SgStatement* function_body = function_definition->get_body();
5847  ASSERT_not_null(function_body);
5848 
5849  SgFunctionParameterList* function_parameter_list = mfuncdecl_stmt->get_parameterList();
5850  ASSERT_not_null(function_parameter_list);
5851 
5852  if (function_body != NULL)
5853  {
5854  // Unparse the tokens from the start of the function declaration to just before the opening "{".
5855 
5856  // DQ (6/5/2021): Note that if the function_definition leading whitespace is not available (e.g. does not exist)
5857  // then nothing will be output. So we have to break this up into two steps.
5858  unparseStatementFromTokenStream (stmt, function_parameter_list, e_token_subsequence_start, e_token_subsequence_end, info);
5859 
5860  // DQ (6/5/2021): If there is any leading whitespace it is associated with the function definition, and not the body (SgBasicBlock).
5861  unparseStatementFromTokenStream (function_definition, e_leading_whitespace_start, e_leading_whitespace_end, info);
5862 
5863  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
5864  unparseStatement(function_body, info);
5865  }
5866  else
5867  {
5868  printf ("We need to handle the case of a function prototype \n");
5869  ROSE_ABORT();
5870  }
5871  return;
5872  }
5873 #endif
5874 
5875  // DQ (12/3/2007): This causes a bug in the output of access level (public, protected, private)
5876  // because the inforamtion change in ninfo is not propogated to info.
5877  // DQ (11/3/2007): Moved construction of ninfo to start of function!
5878  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
5879 
5880  fixupScopeInUnparseInfo (ninfo,mfuncdecl_stmt);
5881 
5882  // Unparse any comments of directives attached to the SgCtorInitializerList
5883  if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_CtorInitializerList() != NULL)
5884  {
5885  unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_CtorInitializerList(), ninfo, PreprocessingInfo::before);
5886  }
5887 
5888  auto const & mfuncdecl_mod = mfuncdecl_stmt->get_functionModifier();
5889  bool isDefaultedOrDeletedMemberFunction = mfuncdecl_mod.isMarkedDefault() || mfuncdecl_mod.isMarkedDelete();
5890  SgFunctionDefinition * mfuncdefn = mfuncdecl_stmt->get_definition();
5891 #if DEBUG_unparseMFuncDeclStmt
5892  printf (" mfuncdecl_stmt->isForward() = %s\n", mfuncdecl_stmt->isForward() ? "true" : "false");
5893  printf (" info.SkipFunctionDefinition() = %s\n", info.SkipFunctionDefinition() ? "true" : "false");
5894  printf (" isDefaultedOrDeletedMemberFunction = %s\n",isDefaultedOrDeletedMemberFunction ? "true" : "false");
5895  printf (" mfuncdecl_stmt->get_definition() = %p = %s\n", mfuncdefn, mfuncdefn ? mfuncdefn->class_name().c_str() : "");
5896 #endif
5897 
5898  // DQ (4/13/2019): If this is a defaulted constructor, then we don't want to unparse the body, so we want to treat it the same as a forward declaration.
5899  if ( !mfuncdecl_stmt->isForward() && mfuncdefn && !ninfo.SkipFunctionDefinition() && isDefaultedOrDeletedMemberFunction == false)
5900  {
5901  unparseStatement(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_definition(), info);
5902  }
5903  else
5904  {
5905  ASSERT_not_null(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_parent());
5906  SgClassDefinition *parent_class = isSgClassDefinition(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_parent());
5907  if (parent_class && parent_class->get_declaration()->get_class_type() == SgClassDeclaration::e_class && !info.skipCheckAccess())
5908  {
5909  info.set_CheckAccess();
5910  }
5911 
5912  unp->u_sage->printSpecifier1(mfuncdecl_stmt, info);
5913 
5914  unp->u_sage->printSpecifier2(mfuncdecl_stmt, info);
5915  info.unset_CheckAccess();
5916 
5917  SgType *rtype = NULL;
5918  unparseReturnType (mfuncdecl_stmt,rtype,ninfo);
5919  ASSERT_not_null(mfuncdecl_stmt);
5920 
5921  ninfo.set_name_qualification_length(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_name_qualification_length());
5922  ninfo.set_global_qualification_required(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_global_qualification_required());

5925  curprint ( nameQualifier.str() );

5927  // DQ (4/2/2018): Adding support for alternative and more sophisticated handling of the function name
5928  // (e.g. with template arguments correctly qualified, etc.).
5929  if (isSgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl(mfuncdecl_stmt) != NULL)
5930  {
5931  unp->u_exprStmt->unparseTemplateMemberFunctionName(isSgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl(mfuncdecl_stmt),ninfo);
5932  }
5933  else
5934  {
5935  curprint ( mfuncdecl_stmt->get_name().str());
5936  }
5937 
5938  SgUnparse_Info ninfo2(info);
5939  ninfo2.set_SkipClassDefinition();
5940  ninfo2.set_SkipEnumDefinition();
5941  ninfo2.set_inArgList();
5942  ninfo2.set_declstatement_ptr(NULL);
5943  ninfo2.set_declstatement_ptr(mfuncdecl_stmt);
5944 
5945  curprint ( string("("));
5946  unparseFunctionArgs(mfuncdecl_stmt, ninfo2);
5947  curprint ( string(")"));
5948 
5949  if (rtype != NULL)

5951  SgUnparse_Info ninfo3(ninfo);

5957 
5958  auto & ctor_inits = mfuncdecl_stmt->get_ctors();

5960  curprint(";");
5961 
5962  } else if (!ctor_inits.empty()) {

5965 #if DEBUG_unparseMFuncDeclStmt

5972  if (it_ctor_init != first) {
5973  curprint(", ");
5974  }
5975  it_ctor_init++;
5976 
5977  unparseAttachedPreprocessingInfo(ctor_init, info, PreprocessingInfo::before);
5978 
5979  SgName nameQualifier = ctor_init->get_qualified_name_prefix();

5983  if (!nameQualifier.is_null()) {
5984  curprint ( nameQualifier.str());
5985  }
5986  curprint(ctor_init->get_name().str());
5987 
5988  SgExpression* initializer = ctor_init->get_initializer();

5990  SgAggregateInitializer * aggr_init = isSgAggregateInitializer(initializer);
5991  SgConstructorInitializer * ctor_init = isSgConstructorInitializer(initializer);
5992  bool output_parenthesis = ctor_init == nullptr;

5994 
5995  bool compiler_generated = initializer->get_startOfConstruct()->isCompilerGenerated();
5996 #if DEBUG_unparseMFuncDeclStmt

6004  unparseExpression(initializer, ninfo2);

6006 
6007  if (output_parenthesis) curprint ( string(")"));
6008  }
6009  }
6010  }

6025 #if DEBUG_unparseMFuncDeclStmt

6031 void
6032 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseTrailingFunctionModifiers(SgMemberFunctionDeclaration* mfuncdecl_stmt, SgUnparse_Info& info)
6033  {
6034  // DQ (9/9/2014): Refactored support for function modifiers.
6035  bool outputRestrictKeyword = false;
6036  SgMemberFunctionType *mftype = isSgMemberFunctionType(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_type());
6037 
6038 #if 0
6039  printf ("In unparseTrailingFunctionModifiers: unparse const,volatile, const volatile, etc. from the SgMemberFunctionType \n");
6040 #endif
6041 
6042  // DQ (9/9/2014): Note this was using info where it was refactored from and ninfo is passed to this function.
6043  if (!info.SkipFunctionQualifier() && mftype )
6044  {
6045  if (mftype->isConstFunc())
6046  {
6047  curprint(" const");
6048  }
6049  if (mftype->isVolatileFunc())
6050  {
6051  curprint(" volatile");
6052  }
6053 
6054  // DQ (12/11/2012): Added support for restrict (in EDG 4.x we want this to be more uniform with "const" and "volatile" modifier handling.
6055  if (mftype->isRestrictFunc())
6056  {
6057 #if 0
6058  printf ("In unparseTrailingFunctionModifiers: unparse restrict keyword from specification in SgMemberFunctionType \n");
6059 #endif
6060  outputRestrictKeyword = true;
6061 
6062  // DQ (12/11/2012): Make sure that this way of specifing the restrict keyword is set.
6063  ROSE_ASSERT (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().get_typeModifier().isRestrict() == true);
6064 
6065  // curprint ( string(" restrict"));
6066  }
6067 
6068  // DQ (1/11/2020): Adding support for lvalue reference member function modifiers.
6069  if (mftype->isLvalueReferenceFunc())
6070  {
6071  curprint(" &");
6072  }
6073 
6074  // DQ (1/11/2020): Adding support for rvalue reference member function modifiers.
6075  if (mftype->isRvalueReferenceFunc())
6076  {
6077  curprint(" &&");
6078  }
6079  }
6080 
6081  // DQ (12/11/2012): Avoid redundant output of the restrict keyword.
6082  // DQ (4/28/2004): Added support for restrict modifier
6083  // if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().get_typeModifier().isRestrict())
6084  if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().get_typeModifier().isRestrict() && (outputRestrictKeyword == false))
6085  {
6086  outputRestrictKeyword = true;
6087 #if 0
6088  printf ("In unparseTrailingFunctionModifiers: unparse restrict keyword from specification in mfuncdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().get_typeModifier() \n");
6089 #endif
6090  // DQ (12/11/2012): Error checking.
6091  if (mftype != NULL)
6092  {
6093  ROSE_ASSERT (mftype->isRestrictFunc() == true);
6094  }
6095 
6096  // curprint ( string(" restrict"));
6097  }
6098 
6099  // DQ (12/11/2012): We have two ways of setting the specification of the restrict keyword, but we only want to output the keyword once.
6100  // This make this code less sensative to which way it is specified and enforces that both ways are set.
6101  // At the moment there are two ways that a member function is marked as restrict:
6102  // 1) Via it's function type modifier (const-volatile modifier)
6103  // 2) The declaration modifier's const-volatile modifier.
6104  // It does not appear that the "restrict" keyword modifies the type of the function (g++ does not allow overloading on restrict, for example).
6105  // Thus if it is not a part of the type then it should be a part of the declaration modifier and not in the SgMemberFunctionType.
6106  // So maybe we should remove it from the SgMemberFunctionType? I am not clear on this design point at present, so we have forced both
6107  // to be set consistantly (and this is handled in the SageBuilder interface), plus a consistancy test in the AST consistancy tests.
6108  // The reason it is in the type modifier held by the declaration modifier is because it is not a prat of the function type (formally).
6109  // But the reason it is a part of the type modifier is because it is used for function parameter types. This design point is
6110  // less than elegant and I'm not clear on what would make this simpler. For the moment we have focused on making it consistant
6111  // across the two ways it can be represented (and fixing the SageBuilder Interface to set it consistantly).
6112  if (outputRestrictKeyword == true)
6113  {
6114  curprint(Unparse_Type::unparseRestrictKeyword());
6115  }
6116 
6117  // DQ (4/28/2004): Added support for throw modifier
6118  if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().isThrow())
6119  {
6120  // Unparse SgThrow
6121 #if 0
6122  printf ("In Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseTrailingFunctionModifiers(): Output throw modifier \n");
6123 #endif
6124  // unparseThrowExp(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_throwExpression,info);
6125  // printf ("Incomplete implementation of throw specifier on function \n");
6126  // curprint ( string(" throw( /* from unparseTrailingFunctionModifiers() type list output not implemented */ )";
6127  const SgTypePtrList& exceptionSpecifierList = mfuncdecl_stmt->get_exceptionSpecification();
6128  // unparseExceptionSpecification(exceptionSpecifierList,ninfo);
6129  unparseExceptionSpecification(exceptionSpecifierList,info);
6130  }
6131 
6132  // if (mfuncdecl_stmt->isPure())
6133  if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_functionModifier().isPureVirtual())
6134  {
6135  // DQ (1/22/2013): Supress the output of the pure virtual syntax if this is the defining declaration (see test2013_26.C).
6136  // curprint ( string(" = 0"));
6137  if (mfuncdecl_stmt != mfuncdecl_stmt->get_definingDeclaration())
6138  {
6139  curprint(" = 0");
6140  }
6141  }
6142 
6143  // DQ (7/9/2022): This can only be output for member function declarations defined in the class.
6144  // DQ (8/11/2014): Added support for final keyword unparsing.
6145  if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().isFinal() == true)
6146  {
6147  // DQ (2/12/2019): Testing, final can't be used on prototypes (I think).
6148  // curprint(" /* output from test 1 */ ");
6149  // curprint(" final");
6150  // DQ (7/10/2022): "final" is not a keyword, but it can only be used like a keyword
6151  // with member function declarations inside of the associated class definition.
6152  // curprint(" override");
6153  SgClassDefinition* parentClassDefinition = isSgClassDefinition(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_parent());
6154  if (parentClassDefinition != NULL && mfuncdecl_stmt->get_scope() == parentClassDefinition)
6155  {
6156  curprint(" final");
6157  }
6158  }
6159 
6160  // DQ (7/9/2022): This can only be output for member function declarations defined in the class.
6161  // DQ (8/11/2014): Added support for final keyword unparsing.
6162  if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_declarationModifier().isOverride() == true)
6163  {
6164  // DQ (7/10/2022): "override" is not a keyword, but it can only be used like a keyword
6165  // with member function declarations inside of the associated class definition.
6166  // curprint(" override");
6167  SgClassDefinition* parentClassDefinition = isSgClassDefinition(mfuncdecl_stmt->get_parent());
6168  if (parentClassDefinition != NULL && mfuncdecl_stmt->get_scope() == parentClassDefinition)
6169  {
6170  curprint(" override");
6171  }
6172  }
6173 
6174  // DQ (4/13/2019): Added support for default keyword unparsing.
6175  if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_functionModifier().isMarkedDefault() == true)
6176  {
6177  curprint(" = default");
6178  }
6179 
6180  // DQ (4/13/2019): Added support for delete keyword unparsing.
6181  if (mfuncdecl_stmt->get_functionModifier().isMarkedDelete() == true)
6182  {
6183  curprint(" = delete");
6184  }
6185  }

7146 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseTypeAttributes ( SgDeclarationStatement* declaration )

7148  // DQ (10/4/2012): Added support for transparent unions.

8422 static bool
8423 isOutputAsmOperand(SgAsmOp* asmOp)
8424  {
8425  // There are two way of evaluating if an SgAsmOp is an output operand,
8426  // depending of if we are using the specific mechanism that knows
8427  // records register details or the more general mechanism that records
8428  // the registers as strings. The string based mechanism lack precision
8429  // and would require parsing to retrive the instruction details, but it
8430  // is instruction set independent. The more precise mechanism records
8431  // the specific register codes and could in the future be interpreted
8432  // to be a part of the binary analysis support in ROSE.
8433 
8434  return (asmOp->get_recordRawAsmOperandDescriptions() == true) ? (asmOp->get_isOutputOperand() == true) : (asmOp->get_modifiers() & SgAsmOp::e_output);
8435  }

8438 static std::string
8439 asm_escapeString(const std::string & s)
8440  {
8441  // DQ (2/4/2014): We need a special version of this function for unparsing the asm strings.
8442  // The version of escapeString in util will expand '\' to be '\\' and this should not

8445  std::string result;
8446  for (size_t i = 0; i < s.length(); ++i)
8447  {
8448  switch (s[i])
8449  {
8450 #if 0
8451  // DQ (2/4/2014): I think this is a problem for asm strings (it translates "\n"
8452  // substrings into "\\\n" substrings which are a problem for the assembler.
8453  case '\\':
8454 #if 1
8455  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing \\\\ character \n");
8456 #endif
8457  result += "\\\\";
8458  break;
8459 #endif
8460  case '"':
8461 #if 0
8462  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing \\\" character \n");
8463 #endif
8464  result += "\\\"";
8465  break;
8466  case '\a':
8467 #if 0
8468  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing \\a character \n");
8469 #endif
8470  result += "\\a";
8471  break;
8472  case '\f':
8473 #if 0
8474  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing \\f character \n");
8475 #endif
8476  result += "\\f";
8477  break;
8478  case '\n':
8479 #if 0
8480  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing \\n character \n");
8481 #endif
8482  result += "\\n";
8483  break;
8484  case '\r':
8485 #if 0
8486  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing \\r character \n");
8487 #endif
8488  result += "\\r";
8489  break;
8490  case '\t':
8491 #if 0
8492  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing \\t character \n");
8493 #endif
8494  result += "\\t";
8495  break;
8496  case '\v':
8497 #if 0
8498  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing \\v character \n");
8499 #endif
8500  result += "\\v";
8501  break;
8502  default:
8503 #if 0
8504  printf ("In asm_escapeString(): processing default case character \n");
8505 #endif
8506  if (isprint(s[i]))
8507  {
8508  result.push_back(s[i]);

8510  else
8511  {

8513  stream << '\\';

8526 void
8527 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseAsmStmt(SgStatement* stmt, SgUnparse_Info& info)
8528  {
8529  // This function is called as part of the handling of the C "asm"
8530  // statement. The "asm" statement supports inline assembly in C.
8531  // These sorts of statements are not common in most user code
8532  // (except embedded code), but are common in many system header files.
8533 
8534  SgAsmStmt* asm_stmt = isSgAsmStmt(stmt);
8535  ASSERT_not_null(asm_stmt);
8536 
8537 #define ASM_DEBUGGING 0
8538 
8539 #if ASM_DEBUGGING
8540  printf ("In unparseAsmStmt(): stmt = %p = %s \n",stmt,stmt->class_name().c_str());
8541 #endif
8542 
8543  // DQ (5/23/2015): The p_skip_unparse_asm_commands data member has been changed to be a static data member
8544  // so that we can support ASM statments hidden in AST islands (AST subtrees hidden in types and thus not
8545  // connected to the AST (since types are shared). The use of the typeof operator in conjunction with the
8546  // GNU statemnet expression can permit this configuration.
8547 
8548  // DQ (5/19/2015): Note that sourceFile will be NULL in the case where the asm statement is in
8549  // a GNU statement expression in a typeof operator. Not clear yet what to do about this case.
8550  // See test2015_141.c for an example of this. One solution might be to make the
8551  // skip_unparse_asm_commands variable a static data member.
8552  // SgSourceFile* sourceFile = TransformationSupport::getSourceFile(stmt);
8553  // ASSERT_not_null(sourceFile);
8554 
8555  // DQ (1/10/2009): The C language ASM statements are providing significant trouble, they are
8556  // frequently machine specific and we are compiling then on architectures for which they were
8557  // not designed. This option allows then to be read, constructed in the AST to support analysis
8558  // but not unparsed in the code given to the backend compiler, since this can fail. (See
8559  // test2007_20.C from Linux Kernel for an example).
8560  // if (sourceFile->get_skip_unparse_asm_commands() == true)
8561  if (SgSourceFile::get_skip_unparse_asm_commands() == true)
8562  {
8563  // This is a case were we skip the unparsing of the C language ASM statements, because while
8564  // we can read then into the AST to support analysis, we can not always output them correctly.
8565  // This subject requires additional work.
8566 
8567  printf ("Warning: Sorry, C language ASM statement skipped (parsed and built in AST, but not output by the code generation phase (unparser)) \n");
8568 
8569  // DQ (10/25/2012): This needs to be made a bit more sophisticated (tailored to the type of associated scope in the source code).
8570  // DQ (10/23/2012): If we skip the ASM statment then include an expression statement to take it's place.
8571  // curprint ( "/* C language ASM statement skipped (in code generation phase) */ ");
8572  // curprint ( "/* C language ASM statement skipped (in code generation phase) */ \"compiled using -rose:skip_unparse_asm_commands\"; ");
8573  SgScopeStatement* associatedScope = stmt->get_scope();
8574  ASSERT_not_null(associatedScope);
8575 
8576  if (associatedScope->containsOnlyDeclarations() == true)
8577  {
8578  // Output a simple string.
8579  curprint ( "/* C language ASM statement skipped (in code generation phase) */ ");
8580  }
8581  else
8582  {
8583  // We might need a expression statement to properly close off another statement (e.g. a "if" statement).
8584  curprint ( "/* C language ASM statement skipped (in code generation phase) */ \"compiled using -rose:skip_unparse_asm_commands\"; ");
8585  }
8586 
8587  return;
8588  }
8589 
8590 #if 0
8591  // DQ (2/4/2014): Note that test2012_175.c demonstrates where EDG causes the IR node in ROSE to be marked
8592  // as volatile and it causes an error in the generated code.
8593 
8594  // DQ (7/23/2006): Added support for volatile as modifier.
8595  if (asm_stmt->get_declarationModifier().get_typeModifier().get_constVolatileModifier().isVolatile())
8596  {
8597 #if ASM_DEBUGGING
8598  curprint("/* output volatile keyword from unparseAsmStmt */ \n ");
8599 #endif
8600  curprint("volatile ");
8601  }
8602 #endif
8603 
8604  // Output the "asm" keyword.
8605  // DQ (8/31/2013): We have to output either "__asm__" or "asm" (for MSVisual C++ I think we might need "__asm").
8606 #if 0
8607  string backEndCompiler = BACKEND_CXX_COMPILER_NAME_WITHOUT_PATH;
8608  if (backEndCompiler == "g++" || backEndCompiler == "gcc" || backEndCompiler == "mpicc" || backEndCompiler == "mpicxx")
8609  {
8610  // curprint("__asm__ ");
8611  curprint("asm ");
8612  }
8613  else
8614  {
8615  curprint("asm ");
8616  }
8617 #else
8618 
8619 // DQ (2/25/2014): Note that the 4.2.4 compiler will define both BACKEND_C_COMPILER_SUPPORTS_ASM and BACKEND_C_COMPILER_SUPPORTS_UNDESCORE_ASM
8620 // So we need to use another macro BACKEND_C_COMPILER_SUPPORTS_LONG_STRING_ASM that will work uniformally on both 4.4.7 and 4.2.4 versions of
8621 // the GNU compiler. This is truely strange behavior.

8946 void
8947 Unparse_ExprStmt::unparseTypeDefStmt(SgStatement* stmt, SgUnparse_Info& info)
8948  {
8949  SgTypedefDeclaration* typedef_stmt = isSgTypedefDeclaration(stmt);
8950  ASSERT_not_null(typedef_stmt);
8951 
8952 #define DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS 0
8953 
8954 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
8955  printf ("TOP of unp->u_type->unparseTypeDefStmt() = %p \n",typedef_stmt);
8956  typedef_stmt->get_file_info()->display("In unp->u_type->unparseTypeDefStmt(): debug");
8957 #endif
8958 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
8959  curprint("\n /* In unp->u_type->unparseTypeDefStmt() */ \n");
8960 #endif
8961 
8962  // DQ (10/5/2004): This is the explicitly set boolean value which indicates that a class declaration is buried inside
8963  // the current variable declaration (e.g. struct A { int x; } a;). In this case we have to output the base type with
8964  // its definition.
8965  bool outputTypeDefinition = typedef_stmt->get_typedefBaseTypeContainsDefiningDeclaration();
8966 
8967 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
8968  printf ("In unparseTypeDefStmt(): typedef_stmt = %p outputTypeDefinition = %s \n",typedef_stmt,(outputTypeDefinition == true) ? "true" : "false");
8969 #endif
8970 
8971  if (!info.inEmbeddedDecl())
8972  {
8973 #if OUTPUT_DEBUGGING_FUNCTION_INTERNALS || 0
8974  curprint("\n/* NOT an embeddedDeclaration */ \n");
8975 #endif
8976  SgClassDefinition *cdefn = isSgClassDefinition(typedef_stmt->get_parent());
8977  if (cdefn && cdefn->get_declaration()->get_class_type() == SgClassDeclaration::e_class)
8978  info.set_CheckAccess();
8979  // printDebugInfo("entering unp->u_sage->printSpecifier", true);
8980  unp->u_sage->printSpecifier(typedef_stmt, info);
8981  info.unset_CheckAccess();
8982  }
8983  else
8984  {
8985 #if OUTPUT_DEBUGGING_FUNCTION_INTERNALS || 0
8986  curprint("\n/* Found an embeddedDeclaration */ \n");
8987 #endif
8988  }
8989 
8990  SgUnparse_Info ninfo(info);
8991 
8992  // DQ (10/10/2006): Do output any qualified names (particularly for non-defining declarations).
8993  // ninfo.set_forceQualifiedNames();
8994 
8995  // DQ (10/5/2004): This controls the unparsing of the class definition
8996  // when unparsing the type within this variable declaration.
8997  if (outputTypeDefinition == true)
8998  {
8999  // printf ("Output the full definition as a basis for the typedef base type \n");
9000  // DQ (10/5/2004): If this is a defining declaration then make sure that we don't skip the definition
9001  ROSE_ASSERT(ninfo.SkipClassDefinition() == false);
9002 
9003  // DQ (12/22/2005): Enum definition should be handled here as well
9004  ROSE_ASSERT(ninfo.SkipEnumDefinition() == false);
9005 
9006  // DQ (10/14/2006): As part of new implementation of qualified names we now default to the generation of all qualified names unless they are skipped.
9007  ninfo.set_SkipQualifiedNames();
9008  // curprint ( string("\n/* Case of typedefs for outputTypeDefinition == true */\n ";
9009  }
9010  else
9011  {
9012  // printf ("Skip output of the full definition as a basis for the typedef base type \n");
9013  // DQ (10/5/2004): If this is a non-defining declaration then skip the definition
9014  ninfo.set_SkipClassDefinition();
9015  ROSE_ASSERT(ninfo.SkipClassDefinition() == true);
9016 
9017  // DQ (12/22/2005): Enum definition should be handled here as well
9018  ninfo.set_SkipEnumDefinition();
9019  ROSE_ASSERT(ninfo.SkipEnumDefinition() == true);
9020 
9021  // DQ (10/14/2006): Force output any qualified names (particularly for non-defining declarations).
9022  // This is a special case for types of variable declarations.
9023  // ninfo.set_forceQualifiedNames();
9024  // curprint ( string("\n/* Case of typedefs, should we forceQualifiedNames -- outputTypeDefinition == false */\n ";
9025  }
9026 
9027  // Note that typedefs of function pointers and member function pointers
9028  // are quite different from ordinary typedefs and so should be handled
9029  // separately.
9030 
9031  // First look for a pointer to a function
9032  SgPointerType* pointerToType = isSgPointerType(typedef_stmt->get_base_type());
9033 
9034  SgFunctionType* functionType = NULL;
9035  if (pointerToType != NULL)
9036  functionType = isSgFunctionType(pointerToType->get_base_type());
9037 
9038  // DQ (2/3/2019): Adding support to unparse SgPointerMemberType with parenthesis now that they have been
9039  // discovered to not be required in the unparse type code for SgPointerMemberType. See Cxx11_tests/test2019_77.C.
9040  SgPointerMemberType* pointerToMemberType = isSgPointerMemberType(typedef_stmt->get_base_type());
9041 
9042  // DQ (9/15/2004): Added to support typedefs of member pointers
9043  SgMemberFunctionType* pointerToMemberFunctionType = isSgMemberFunctionType(typedef_stmt->get_base_type());
9044 
9045  // DQ (2/14/2019): Adding name qualification support for C++11 enum declarations in typedef types.
9046  SgEnumType* enumType = isSgEnumType(typedef_stmt->get_base_type());
9047  if (enumType != NULL)
9048  {
9049  SgDeclarationStatement* declarationReference = typedef_stmt->get_declaration();
9050  ASSERT_not_null(declarationReference);
9051  SgEnumDeclaration* enumDeclaration = isSgEnumDeclaration(declarationReference);
9052  ASSERT_not_null(enumDeclaration);
9053  SgEnumDeclaration* definingEnumDeclaration = isSgEnumDeclaration(enumDeclaration->get_definingDeclaration());
9054 
9055 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9056  printf ("enumDeclaration->get_name() = %s \n",enumDeclaration->get_name().str());
9057 #endif
9058 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9059  curprint ( string("\n/* In unparseTypeDefStmt: enum name = ") + enumDeclaration->get_name().str() + " */ \n ");
9060  curprint ( string("\n/* In unparseTypeDefStmt: enumDeclaration != definingEnumDeclaration = ") + ((enumDeclaration != definingEnumDeclaration) ? "true" : "false") + " */ \n ");
9061 #endif
9062  // DQ (2/20/2019): If this is not the defining declaration referenced through the declarationReference then use
9063  // the usual method for name qualification via the base type.
9064  if (enumDeclaration != definingEnumDeclaration)
9065  {
9066 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9067  printf ("internal declarationReference != definingEnumDeclaration: so use the name qualification via the base type \n");
9068 #endif
9069  enumType = NULL;
9070  }
9071  else
9072  {
9073  // If this is the defining declaration, then if it is an anonymous class then output as a type.
9074 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9075  printf ("enumDeclaration->get_name() = %s \n",enumDeclaration->get_name().str());
9076 #endif
9077  bool isAnonymousName = (string(enumDeclaration->get_name()).substr(0,14) == "__anonymous_0x");
9078  if (isAnonymousName == true)
9079  {
9080 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9081  printf ("internal declarationReference == definingEnumDeclaration: isAnonymousName == true: so output enum declaration via the base type \n");
9082 #endif
9083  enumType = NULL;
9084  }
9085  }
9086  }
9087 
9088  // DQ (2/18/2019): Adding name qualification support for class declarations in typedef types (declared in other scopes).
9089  SgClassType* classType = isSgClassType(typedef_stmt->get_base_type());
9090  if (classType != NULL)
9091  {
9092  SgDeclarationStatement* declarationReference = typedef_stmt->get_declaration();
9093  ASSERT_not_null(declarationReference);
9094  SgClassDeclaration* classDeclaration = isSgClassDeclaration(declarationReference);
9095  ASSERT_not_null(classDeclaration);
9096  SgClassDeclaration* definingClassDeclaration = isSgClassDeclaration(classDeclaration->get_definingDeclaration());
9097 
9098 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9099  printf ("classDeclaration->get_name() = %s \n",classDeclaration->get_name().str());
9100 #endif
9101 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9102  curprint ( string("\n/* In unparseTypeDefStmt: class name = ") + classDeclaration->get_name().str() + " */ \n ");
9103  curprint ( string("\n/* In unparseTypeDefStmt: classDeclaration != definingClassDeclaration = ") + ((classDeclaration != definingClassDeclaration) ? "true" : "false") + " */ \n ");
9104 #endif
9105  // DQ (2/20/2019): If this is not the defining declaration referenced through the declarationReference then use
9106  // the usual method for name qualification via the base type.
9107  if (classDeclaration != definingClassDeclaration)
9108  {
9109 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9110  printf ("internal declarationReference != definingClassDeclaration: so use the name qualification via the base type \n");
9111 #endif
9112  classType = NULL;
9113  }
9114  else
9115  {
9116  // If this is the defining declaration, then if it is an anonymous class then output as a type.
9117 #if DEBUG_TYPEDEF_DECLARATIONS
9118  printf ("classDeclaration->get_name() = %s \n",classDeclaration->get_name().str());
9119 #endif
9120  bool isAnonymousName = (string(classDeclaration->get_name()).substr(0,14) == "__anonymous_0x");

9941 std::string
9942 replaceString(std::string subject, const std::string& search, const std::string& replace)
9943  {
9944  size_t pos = 0;
9945  while((pos = subject.find(search, pos)) != std::string::npos)
9946  {
9947  subject.replace(pos, search.length(), replace);
9948  pos += replace.length();
9949  }
9950 
9951  return subject;
9952  }

9989  {

9996  SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration* templateFunctionDeclaration = isSgTemplateFunctionDeclaration(stmt);
9997  SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration* templateMemberFunctionDeclaration = isSgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration(stmt);
9998  SgTemplateVariableDeclaration* templateVariableDeclaration = isSgTemplateVariableDeclaration(stmt);
9999  SgTemplateTypedefDeclaration* templateTypedefDeclaration = isSgTemplateTypedefDeclaration(stmt);
10000 
10001  ROSE_ASSERT(
10002  templateClassDeclaration != nullptr ||
10003  templateFunctionDeclaration != nullptr ||
10004  templateMemberFunctionDeclaration != nullptr ||
10005  templateVariableDeclaration != nullptr ||
10006  templateTypedefDeclaration != nullptr
10007  );
10008 
10009  // Unparsing template from the AST can be controlled at the sourcefile or declaration level (for functions and method only)
10010

10012  bool unparse_template_from_ast = sourcefile != NULL && sourcefile->get_unparse_template_ast();
10013  unparse_template_from_ast |= ((templateFunctionDeclaration != NULL) && (templateFunctionDeclaration->get_unparse_template_ast() == true));
10014  unparse_template_from_ast |= ((templateMemberFunctionDeclaration != NULL) && (templateMemberFunctionDeclaration->get_unparse_template_ast() == true));

10018  if (templateMemberFunctionDeclaration) {

10020  } else if (templateVariableDeclaration) {
10021  ROSE_ASSERT(templateVariableDeclaration->get_variables().size() == 1);
10022  auto * iname = templateVariableDeclaration->get_variables()[0];
10023  assoc_tpl_class_decl = iname->get_scope() ? isSgTemplateClassDeclaration(iname->get_scope()->get_parent()) : nullptr;
10024  } else if (templateClassDeclaration || templateTypedefDeclaration) {
10025  assoc_tpl_class_decl = template_stmt->get_scope() ? isSgTemplateClassDeclaration(template_stmt->get_scope()->get_parent()) : nullptr;
10026  }
10027 // std::cout << "assoc_tpl_class_decl = " << std::hex << assoc_tpl_class_decl << " : " << (assoc_tpl_class_decl ? assoc_tpl_class_decl->class_name() : "") << std::endl;

10031  // FIXME unparse nested headers in the wrong order

10034  assoc_tpl_class_decl = assoc_tpl_class_decl->get_scope() ? isSgTemplateClassDeclaration(assoc_tpl_class_decl->get_scope()->get_parent()) : nullptr;
10035  }

10041 
10042  if (templateClassDeclaration != NULL) {

10044  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(NULL);
10045  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(templateClassDeclaration);
10046

10048  if (class_defn != NULL) {
10049  unparseClassDefnStmt(templateClassDeclaration->get_definition(), ninfo);

10051  SgClassDeclaration::class_types class_type = templateClassDeclaration->get_class_type();
10052  switch (class_type) {
10053  case SgClassDeclaration::e_class: curprint("class "); break;
10054  case SgClassDeclaration::e_struct: curprint("struct "); break;
10055  case SgClassDeclaration::e_union: curprint("union "); break;
10056  case SgClassDeclaration::e_template_parameter: curprint(" "); break;

10064  curprint(class_name.getString().c_str());
10065  }
10066 
10067  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(NULL);
10068 
10069  if (!info.SkipSemiColon()) curprint(";");
10070 
10071  } else if (templateFunctionDeclaration != NULL || templateMemberFunctionDeclaration != NULL) {
10072  SgFunctionDeclaration * functionDeclaration = (SgFunctionDeclaration *)stmt;
10073 
10074  SgType * rtype = functionDeclaration->get_type()->get_return_type();
10075  unparseReturnType (functionDeclaration,rtype,ninfo);
10076 
10077  ninfo.unset_SkipSemiColon();
10078  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(NULL);
10079  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(functionDeclaration);
10080 
10081  unparse_helper(functionDeclaration, ninfo);
10082 
10083  ninfo.set_declstatement_ptr(NULL);
10084 
10085  if (rtype != NULL) {
10086  SgUnparse_Info ninfo3(ninfo);
10087  ninfo3.set_isTypeSecondPart();
10088 
10089  unp->u_type->unparseType(rtype, ninfo3);

10091

10094  }
10095 
10096  SgFunctionDefinition * functionDefn = functionDeclaration->get_definition();
10097  if (functionDefn != NULL) {

10099  unparseStatement(body, info);
10100  }
10101 
10102  if (functionDefn == NULL && !info.SkipSemiColon()) curprint(";");
10103 
10104  } else if (templateVariableDeclaration != NULL) {

10108  ROSE_ABORT();
10109  }
